chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Fadl from Ibn Bukayr from Hamzah ibn Humran and Al-Hasan ibn Ziyad said: We entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and there were people with him, so he led them in the Asr prayer. We had already prayed, and we counted for him in his bowing 'Subhana Rabbiya al-Azim' forty or thirty-three times. One of them said in his narration: 'Wa bihamdihi' in bowing and prostration.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: The principle in congregational prayer is lightening (shortening), and in this narration, the reason may be that the people he led were capable of prolonging and strong in it, so for that reason, he (peace be upon him) did that.

key_terms.سُبْحَانَ رَبِّيَ الْعَظِيمُ: Glory be to my Lord, the Magnificent
key_terms.صَلَّى بِهِمُ الْعَصْرَ: He led them in the Asr prayer

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the length of congregational prayer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the flexibility of the Imam in congregational prayer, balancing the general principle of *takhfif* (lightening) with the allowance for *tawil* (prolonging) when the congregation is capable. It underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the Imam's role in adapting worship to the physical and spiritual capacity of the followers, ensuring both devotion and ease.
